note: Three small primitive camping loops spread over the area, each a gravel loop or spur road in oak-hickory timber with pull-ins and, on the area map, a privy. The central one is just north of Route A beside a gravel lot and a pond, on the side of the area where the trails are open to horses. The south one is in the woods above 192-acre Indian Creek Community Lake, about 150 m from the water with no view through the timber; the north one circles a wooded knob at the head of 18-acre Pike's Lake, by the dam. The loops are about two miles apart by air and reached from different county roads. The brochure speaks of camping in self-contained units and says drinking water is not provided. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - three Camping Area symbols on the 2026 map, three GIS points, each a real gravel camping loop in timber on imagery. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. No horse camp is labelled. The three loops are 3.0-3.6 km from the pinned one on separate roads: split lead. Pin (central loop) and phone fine.
flags: INCLUSION (stays): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'. The brochure: 'Overnight camping in self-contained units is permitted only in designated areas, except during firearms deer and spring turkey seasons when all parking areas may be used. Drinking water, electric hookups and toilet facilities are not provided' and 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map.' The map (updated 9/21/2026) draws three Camping Area symbols, each grouped with a Privy and Parking symbol (the north one also a Picnic Area, the south one ADA Parking). GIS layer 27 has three points (OBJECTIDs 227 central, 228 south, 372 north). On the 260 m leaf-on frames each is a gravel loop or looped spur in closed timber with short gravel pull-ins showing through the canopy: the central loop about 60 m across just west of a gravel lot; the south one a spur with a turnaround and three or four angled pull-ins; the north one a loop about 50 m across around a wooded knob with a second gravel loop and lot 60 m north-east. Pad lengths cannot be measured under the leaves; 'self-contained units' in the brochure says RVs are expected. The brochure's 'toilet facilities are not provided' is older than the map, which shows privies.

HORSE CAMP: none is labelled on the page, brochure or map. Horseback riding is 'permitted only on designated multi-use trails north of Hwy' A ('Over 18 miles of trails and interior roads north of Hwy. A have been designated as horse trails'; 'Manure and straw from trailers should be raked from parking area into surrounding grass'), so riders use the parking areas north of Route A; the central and north camping loops are on that side, the south one is not. Nothing marks any loop as equestrian.

CLUSTERS / SPLIT LEAD: three separate camping loops. Central (the stored pin) 39.92709,-93.70147, off Route A. South 39.90103,-93.69111, 3,032 m from the pin, on the road to the east side of Indian Creek Community Lake (the map shows it off CR 510). North 39.95208,-93.67554, 3,555 m from the pin, at Pike's Lake near the CR 500 / CR 519 corner. Each has its own access road from a different county road and each is a loop, not a single small lot, so the two outer ones meet the split test; no other database entry lies within 6 km of the pin. None is plainly the main camp - the south one is nearest the big lake and its ramp, dock and fish-cleaning station. If split: the south loop is not waterfront (timber between it and the lake on every side, nearest water about 150 m); the north loop's road comes within 10-20 m of Pike's Lake on its south side, but the frame is leaf-on and I could not see where the spots are or whether they see the water - by the default-down rule it would be not waterfront, or lakeview only after a leaf-off look.
PIN: stored 39.92709,-93.70147 is the GIS point in the middle of the central loop, under canopy but ringed by the loop road at about 20-30 m; it marks the camp correctly. No move.

ACCESS: 'From Chillicothe, take Highway 190 west 5 miles, then Route A north 5 miles. At the Route W junction, continue on Route A west 1 mile to the area entrance.' The map legend distinguishes Improved Road from Service Road, and all three loops show as gravel roads on imagery. No ford, low-water crossing, 4WD wording or posted limit on the page, brochure or map.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront - stands for the pinned loop): a pond lies about 100 m north of the central loop across the lot and a mown strip, with the loop itself in closed timber; the pond is far too small for a view value in any case.
PHONE: stored 660-646-6122 matches the area page ('For more information call (660) 646-6122').
